name: manual_d74d82
claim: A custom undici connect.lookup callback must handle BOTH dns.lookup callback forms -- (err, address, family) AND, when options.all is true, (err, [{address, family}, ...]) -- because Node 22's net.Socket.connect requests Happy-Eyeballs-style lookups (options.all===true) for any HOSTNAME target. IP-literal targets never invoke connect.lookup at all, so tests using only IP literals will pass while every real hostname-based request throws 'Invalid IP address: undefined' in production.
conditions: hostname vs IP literal test gap

decisions.notes: Found on Claude-Desktop-LLM's endpoint-policy.ts pinnedDispatcher: the connect-time IP-pinning mechanism (built to close a DNS-rebinding TOCTOU gap) only implemented the bare (address, family) callback form. This broke every real request through the documented DEFAULT config (OLLAMA_URL=http://localhost:11434, a hostname) end-to-end against live Ollama, while 64/64 unit tests stayed green because every existing ephemeral-server test used a 127.0.0.1 IP literal, which Node's net module never routes through connect.lookup in the first place. Only surfaced when manually driving the actual compiled server over real stdio against a live local model -- confirms that policy/security code doing custom DNS/connection interception needs at least one hostname-target integration test, not just IP-literal unit tests.
